endorsements.quote: Meaningful integration of youth perspectives, from diverse backgrounds and with a range of needs, should occur throughout the full development cycle, from design to implementation and evaluation.

Only with this collaborative approach—in every step of the process, from design to evaluation—can digital technologies align with real needs and work toward realizing a vision of a society where everybody can fully enjoy their human rights and thrive.
Many researchers in our YouthDMH Delphi poll (CA23153) identified a lack of clear guidance on reimbursing young people appropriately, generating anxiety about coercion and risk [ 45 ].

unlisted_practices: Researchers should explicitly specify and justify the participatory model used (e.g., co-design, PPI, participatory design) and the level of influence young people are expected to have.
Studies should map and document youth involvement across the research life cycle, and should not present involvement limited to early ideation or usability testing as co-design.
Researchers should report what decisions young people influenced and how their input changed the research or intervention, not just participation.
Funders and institutions should require dedicated, justified budget lines for participatory work and assess participation plans as part of funding decisions.
Ethics committees should adopt proportionality-based approaches that require researchers to justify excluding young people, and should distinguish forms of participation when assessing safeguarding.
Establish youth advisory panels, deliberative forums, or youth citizen assemblies to inform regulatory, ethical, and design standards for GenAI systems.
Ensure active involvement of marginalized communities and young people with lived experience in AI policy development and regulation.
Provide independent scrutiny of GenAI system behavior and clearer youth safety standards.
Journals and funders should strengthen reporting expectations requiring transparent reporting of participatory methods and their impact.
Develop ethical guidelines for the participation of young people in digital youth mental health research.
Adopt flexible, tiered consent models where lower-risk youth engagement relies primarily on youth assent and higher-risk engagement requires additional parental involvement.
Train clinicians, youth workers, and professionals to build confidence in participatory approaches with young people.

screen.reason: This is a Viewpoint paper offering recommendations and frameworks for closing the youth participation gap in digital mental health and generative AI research, design, and governance.
